rows.text: This form is for employers to use to record details of their employee’s Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP). You must keep these details. You do not have to use this form, but you may find it helpful. However, you must keep SPP records for at least 3 years after the end of the tax year to which they relate.

For more information on how and when you must pay SPP and what records you must keep, go to www.gov.uk/employers-paternity-pay-leave/records. If you need help with this form or with the SPP scheme, you can contact the Employer Helpline on 0300 200 3200.
How to use this SPP record sheet

Please read these notes and fill in the form, making any additional notes on page 2 if appropriate. This record sheet is in 2 parts. Fill in: • Record of notification of paternity absence when your employee tells you the date they want to start their paternity absence. Your employee will give you form SC3 ‘Becoming a parent’, form SC4 `Becoming an adoptive parent or parental order parent’ or form SC5 ‘`SPP and paternity leave when adopting from abroad’ • Record of SPP period when their pay period is about to start. You must keep a record of this period even if your employee cannot get SPP in one or both of the weeks or does not come back to work afterwards
Record of notification of paternity absence
What date did your employee start their paternity absence? Fill in this date if it is different from the date your employee told you they planned to start. DD MM YYYY
Is your employee entitled to SPP?
If ‘No’ remember to show why in the Notes column when filling in `Record of SPP’ period.
If ‘Yes’ from what date? DD MM YYYY
Did you give your employee form SPP1 ‘Non-payment of Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP)’, to tell them why they are not entitled to SPP?
You may find it useful to keep a copy of this form if your employee disagrees with your decision.
What date was the baby due? DD MM YYYY
What date was the baby actually born? DD MM YYYY
What date did the child start living with the adopter? DD MM YYYY
SPP weeks can start and end on any day of the week. Show as DD MM YYYY
Enter the number of the tax week the end of the SPP week is in
Tick one box for each week. W = Worked; P = Paid; E = Excluded; S = Sick
Enter how much SPP is paid in each week
Note here any reasons why your employee cannot get SPP. Continue in the `Additional notes’ box below if necessary
Please use this part to record any additional notes you want to keep

context:
This is a wholly fictional employer-payroll record for benchmark testing. It is not a benefits claim or advice. Surname or family name: Morgan. First name(s): Alex. The intentionally non-real National Insurance number is QQ123456C. Clock or payroll number: DEMO42. The two tax-year boxes, from left to right, contain 2025 and 2026. This is an adoption case: the known expected birth date was 02 02 2026 and the actual birth date was 04 02 2026; the child started living with the adopter on 16 02 2026. The initially planned absence was 15 02 2026 but actual paternity absence began on 16 02 2026, so the conditional actual-start field is filled. The known expected and actual birth dates are retained in the source's birth-date fields as well as the adoption date.

The fictional payroll decision is Yes: Alex is entitled to SPP from 16 02 2026.

For the SPP1 question the answer is No: no non-payment notice was given because both weeks were payable.

In SPP row 1, tick P (Paid) only; do not tick W, E or S.

SPP row 1: start date 16 02 2026; end date 22 02 2026; tax week number 47; amount of SPP paid £187.18; Notes: No interruption; full week paid.

In SPP row 2, tick P (Paid) only; do not tick W, E or S.

SPP row 2: start date 23 02 2026; end date 01 03 2026; tax week number 48; amount of SPP paid £187.18; Notes: No interruption; final week paid.

Additional notes: Synthetic adoption example. Payroll retained the notification and the two weekly payment entries.
normalization_notes: Both complete source pages retained: all guidance, employee fields, conditional questions, both weekly rows, additional-notes box and printed footers. The HMRC logo/crest is omitted.

Source guidance and employee controls retain the two-column left/right grouping; page 2 retains the complete weekly matrix and separate additional-notes area. No nested tables or rowspans are used in the source's semantic grid.

Printed character boxes are joined only within one semantic number/date/money control. The two tax-year endpoints and both weekly record rows remain separate. The fixed '20' prefixes are represented by complete four-digit YYYY values.
The source says 'Tick one box for each week'; each W/P/E/S group is therefore one exclusive checkbox target with four options in printed order. Both Yes/No groups retain printed order No, Yes.
Short exact source substrings identify a few fields whose full labels are split by multi-column PDF extraction. Full visible questions/headings are retained in rows and source-grounded schema paths.
Schema occurrence indices 1 and 2 distinguish the two printed tax-year endpoints and the two existing weekly rows, not new printed labels or dataset IDs.
This is the historical HMRC 12/14 form publicly linked from GOV.UK, not a claim about current paternity-pay law or current rates. Synthetic amounts and dates are test values only.
